summary.text: A neural network for recognizing handwritten digits is built from layers of neurons holding activations between 0 and 1, connected by roughly 13,000 weights and biases that learning adjusts.

source_refs.quote: put together a neural network that can learn to recognize handwritten digits
this network has almost exactly 13,000 total weights and biases

key_points.text: A neuron is simply a thing that holds a number between 0 and 1, and that number is called its activation.

source_refs.quote: a thing that holds a number, specifically a number between 0 and 1
This number inside the neuron is called its activation

key_points.text: The input layer has one neuron per pixel of the 28x28 image, 784 in total, and the output layer has ten, one per digit.

source_refs.quote: 784 neurons in total
this has 10 neurons, each representing one of the digits

key_points.text: Activations in one layer determine the activations of the next, and that is the whole information-processing mechanism.

source_refs.quote: activations in one layer determine the activations of the next layer

key_points.text: Every connection carries a weight, and every neuron adds a bias that sets how high its weighted sum must be before it activates.

source_refs.quote: assign a weight to each one of the connections
the bias tells you how high the weighted sum needs to be before the neuron starts getting meaningfully active

key_points.text: The sigmoid function squashes an unbounded weighted sum back into the range between 0 and 1.

source_refs.quote: the sigmoid function, also known as a logistic curve
pump this weighted sum into some function that squishes the real number line

key_points.text: Learning means getting the computer to find a valid setting for all of those weights and biases.

source_refs.quote: when we talk about learning, what that's referring to is getting the computer to find a valid setting

important_details.text: The demonstrated network uses two hidden layers of sixteen neurons each, which the presenter calls an arbitrary choice.

source_refs.quote: two hidden layers, each one with 16 neurons
that's kind of an arbitrary choice

important_details.text: Pixel grayscale values run from 0 for black up to 1 for white.

source_refs.quote: ranging from 0 for black pixels up to 1 for white pixels

important_details.text: Weight grids are drawn with green pixels for positive weights and red for negative ones.

source_refs.quote: green pixels to indicate positive weights, and red pixels to indicate negative weights

important_details.text: The network's answer is whichever neuron in the output layer is brightest.

source_refs.quote: the brightest neuron of that output layer is the network's choice

important_details.text: Written compactly, one layer transition is a matrix-vector product plus a bias vector, wrapped in a sigmoid.

source_refs.quote: organize all of the weights as a matrix
adding the entire vector to the previous matrix vector product
